stories.title: The clearing remembers
stories.opening: The stream kept its own time. Wilson had been at the clearing since the first light reached the old stones, his axe rising and falling over ground worn by years of practice. Jake had come for quiet, not company. He stopped when four hooves turned toward him. The water went on moving. Neither mentioned the lake or the carnival until Wilson broke the silence. “You picked a fine morning to interrupt.” Jake glanced at the space between the boulders. “I was looking for somewhere nobody wanted anything.” Wilson raised his axe. “Then you took the wrong path.”
povs: CHAR-WILSON-LOOK
Public defeat prompts private practice; sees intrusion as another test, not knowledge of Jake's motives.
CHAR-JAKE-KALOPER
Seeks solitude after carnival defeat; recognizes challenge and chooses whether to engage.
stories.pressure: P10 opposing silhouettes, axe and lightsaber, clear ground between stream and old ruins; no decisive strike yet.
stories.home: DK wins the duel; ObiWan survives. Injury specifics remain held; no belt or permanent state transfer.
stories.away: ObiWan wins the duel; DK survives. Injury specifics remain held; no belt or territorial claim.
stories.continuity: W11 bridge and carnival remain elsewhere; four-hoof identity, hood and clipped saber before challenge.

stories.title: The bank knows its own
stories.opening: Mist covered the water, but it could not hide the old boards of the hunting cabin. One newer plank lay among the dark timber of the dock; the half-sunken boat still pulled gently at its tether. Bobby waited on the raised bank. Phillip approached with three heads watching the cabin, water and ground in turn, all carried by one body. “After last week, you must be feeling dangerous.” Bobby gave him a long look. “You came all this way to ask?” The water moved beneath the dock. Phillip had expected a short visit; the swamp had offered no such promise.
povs: CHAR-BOBBY-MITCHELL
External observable posture and territorial familiarity; no unlicensed interior monologue.
CHAR-PHILLIP-PITTS
Confidence and postseason ambition; three viewpoints must coordinate one body's choices.
stories.pressure: P13 confrontation uses the same bank, dock and waterline; environmental challenge or combat remains subject to exact action review.

stories.away: TDS earns victory by overcoming the challenge without repeating Chins' wrong-turn plot; no invented injury or elimination.

stories.title: A toast in the hills
stories.opening: The cabin windows were warm against the cold hillside. Zach shook the wind from his shoulders and accepted the invitation without a purchase agreement. Kevin had set two glasses on the old table. “To the chairman,” he said. “And to David, wherever he's found a chair.” Zach laughed. “Preferably one with a view.” They toasted victories and the peculiar trouble of winning an argument with Babb. A gust struck the shutters. Kevin looked toward the room's far side, then back at his guest. Zach noticed the pause, but not its meaning. The evening had begun courteously enough.
povs: CHAR-KEVIN-ZEEK
Hosts celebration and conceals his fictional intent; rivalry memory does not establish a historical cabin event.
CHAR-ZACH-WILSON
Accepts invitation in good faith; observes hesitation and remains alert, no knowledge of LLC private meeting.
stories.pressure: P16 toast becomes uneasy, use table/hearth/windows from stable interior; deceptive intent abstract only.
stories.home: Red's fictional deception succeeds, Duckhook confined as requested; no mechanism, durable confinement or future availability lock without later continuity ruling.
stories.away: Duckhook recognizes the deception and avoids it; no automatic change in corporate position.
stories.continuity: W11 corporate takeover selected fiction; W8 Red loss and prior competitive memories, no unsupported personal quotations; G05 parallel but private.

stories.title: The good table
stories.opening: Jordan had set the table long before the guest arrived. The old garden beds were neat, the covered gathering area ready, and the Dutch oven stood near the fire. The television carried the afternoon's football conversation into the yard. Brandon arrived on Dark Horse, greeted his host and looked over the spread. “You expecting the whole conference?” Jordan handed him a drink. “Only the part that knows how football works.” Brandon glanced at the screen. “Then you're going to have to explain why you're on that side of the argument.” The meal was ready. The conversation was not.
povs: CHAR-JORDAN-HOLLINGSHEAD
Pride in prepared hospitality; W11 delivery lesson tempers performance until rivalry rises.
CHAR-BRANDON-PRYOR
Guest enters with W11 confidence and challenges host's football judgment; no real-owner political/sport opinions attributed.

stories.away: Chili wins; table upset and Dark Horse hoof marks as fictional temporary gag, no permanent damage.
stories.continuity: Modern fixtures scoped; mature garden and ordinary private gathering; no invented historical awards or riding approach.

stories.title: The other office
stories.opening: Babb had not brought Austin to Jackson. The old records in this room had outlasted more than one arrangement, and the desk had no new name on it. Duckhook's place on the rival board was unmistakable. The reigning champion regarded it without removing the Belt. “You invited me here to talk about Zach?” Babb opened a folder. “I invited you to talk about the next time one of us sees him.” He let the offer rest between them. Austin looked at the papers, then at Babb. “And what do you expect in return?” Neither had yet agreed to anything.
povs: CHAR-DAVID-BABB
Seeks leverage after W11 Jackson ouster; old archive represents agency beyond office title.
CHAR-AUSTIN-BYARS
Weighs fictional alliance while retaining Belt; no knowledge of Red's cabin invitation.

stories.home: LLC wins, both appear pleased with conditional alliance; no guaranteed future opponent or asset transfer in canon.

stories.title: What the road remembers
stories.opening: The early light had scarcely reached the trees when rain began to darken the track. Ben knew what a familiar road could become in weather. Last week's wrong turn had taught him that recognition was not the same as certainty. From the truck he watched the verge disappear into mist, then glanced back toward the road he could still recognize. A gust shook leaves from the branches. He had started the morning convinced that he had somewhere to be. Now the weather was asking whether the road would let him get there.
povs: CHAR-BEN-WHIPPLE
Confidence becomes measured caution after W11 wrong turn; no island destination confirmed.
CHAR-MANNING-WELTY
External elemental weather only; rain, wind and visibility constrain progress, no internal voice.

stories.home: El Niño wins; progress stops or Ben turns back, no crash, elimination or permanent road closure.
stories.away: Chins wins; truck clears affected stretch, not confirmed Playoff Island admission.
